children: O’Reilly’s third-quarter sales and net income increased year over year, as comparable-store growth and sales from new stores lifted results. Gross margin also improved, supported by tariff refunds, better acquisition costs in select categories and distribution-cost leverage; higher interest expense partly offset operating gains.
¹ Reported as “Sales”. ² Reported as “Net income”. ³ Reported as “Earnings per share-assuming dilution”.
: Comparable store sales rose 7.2%, driven by higher average tickets for DIY and professional customers and more professional-customer transactions.
: The company opened 63 net new stores in the quarter and expects 225 to 235 net openings in 2026.
: Gross profit reached 52.4% of sales, up from 51.9%, aided by tariff refunds and improved acquisition costs for select product categories.
: SG&A declined to 30.9% of sales from 31.1%, principally reflecting leverage of store operating costs on strong comparable sales.
